title: Find and remove the cause of the longer checks stage
summary: Athena's checks stage median rose from 0.2 to 0.6 min per landed job. Find the cause in the checks path (routing, CI result reuse, baseline lookup, executor), state it in a docs/design note, and fix it so the stage gets shorter. The audience is the maintainer reading the next throughput review.

defaults_applied.how: Fix is Rust code in crates/.
Criterion requires cargo test and clippy to pass with a test for the fix.
The cause must be found and removed, not worked around.
Test criterion checks the fixed behavior by running cargo test.
The goal is a shorter checks stage, so the cause is stated with evidence.
One focused fix plus one note.
The design note is written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs (SnapExec runs one routed check after a one-time disk gate; baseline lookup uses RefuseExec and WaitsWhileRunning, with a bounded CI read loop in crates/athena-core/src/ci_result.rs). Related, not yet read: crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (stage medians). No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected.

The exact cause is not known from the request. The producer must find it by reading the checks path (what a check runs, CI result reuse versus local runs, baseline wait bound, snapshot restore after each check) and recent changes to it, and must measure it directly, not through a stand-in.
The change is a single focused fix plus a short note in docs/design/ stating the cause with evidence; no refusal rule is added or tightened.
The next throughput review cannot be run in the job; the verifier checks that the change removes work or waiting from the checks path, not the future median.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not expected to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A note under docs/design/ (or the change's commit text/doc comment) states the cause of the longer checks stage, citing the specific crates/ code path and the evidence (measured or labeled estimate).
The diff to crates/ removes or bounds the identified cause (extra check run, wait, repeated work or snapshot restore) in the checks path, rather than a symptom such as raising a limit.
A new or updated test in crates/ exercises the fixed behavior, failing on the old behavior; run `cargo test` and it passes.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
Existing checks behavior is preserved: the same routed checks still run and failures still hold or reject the job; existing tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs still pass.

out_of_scope: Changing other stages (planning, producer, verification) that did not grow
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflow files
Changing how throughput medians are computed or reported
departures: The cause is unknown and needs investigation, so cost and wall time are somewhat above the reference, and acceptance is less certain.
urgent_reason: Removes extra time in the checks stage, so each job spends less time waiting on checks.
